essence: Former non-being, being, action — things always, suddenly here, middle-formed and confused: whence their truth? In the non-true, unsteady, manifold, clever dream-delusion — transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning's contriving: awakened, become. Things lack truth; the only response is awakening.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of awakening (prabodha); the vyabhicāri is clarity (prasāda) of transcending the four fetters. The rasa is the tranquility of awakening — not the thrill of argument but the peace of seeing things as non-true and waking up.
